units.source_text: “又如写字，并无精深修养，只是挥毫泼墨，装点得锋芒毕露，神气活现；

en.t: Take calligraphy, for example: without any deep cultivation, one may simply flourish the brush and splash the ink, dressing it up so that every sharp edge stands out and the whole thing seems full of spirit;

units.source_text: 约略看来，这真是才气横溢、风韵潇洒的墨宝。

en.t: At a rough glance, it truly looks like a treasured piece of writing overflowing with talent and graceful charm.

units.source_text: 反之，真才实学之书家，着墨不多，外表并不触目；

en.t: By contrast, a calligrapher of genuine talent and solid learning uses little ink, and the outward appearance does not particularly catch the eye;

units.source_text: 但倘将两者共陈并列，再度比较观看，则后者自属优胜。

en.t: but if the two are set out side by side and examined again in comparison, the latter is naturally the superior one.
